record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Let γ be a closed strictly convex hypersurface in R^n, and let Π be the phase cylinder of the billiard inside γ, viewed as an open symplectic manifold of oriented lines intersecting γ transversally at two points. Given ε > 0 and k ∈ N, is every C∞ Hamiltonian symplectomorphism Π → Π a C∞ limit of compositions of reflections from γ and from hypersurfaces that are ε-close to γ in the C^k topology, using reflections only and not their inverses?

evidence.quote: Question [14, subsection 1.6]: Is it true that for every given ε > 0 and k ∈ N each C∞-smooth Hamiltonian symplectomorphism Π → Π is the C∞-limit of compositions of reflections from the hypersurface γ and from hypersurfaces ε-close to γ in the C^k-topology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a closed, strictly convex, $C^\infty$-smooth hypersurface. Consider the space of oriented straight lines in $\mathbb{R}^n$ that intersect $\gamma$ transversally at exactly two points; this space, denoted $\Pi$ and called the phase cylinder of the billiard inside $\gamma$, is an open symplectic manifold (carrying the symplectic form induced from the standard one on the space of oriented lines in $\mathbb{R}^n$).

For any $C^\infty$ closed hypersurface $\sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ that is sufficiently close to $\gamma$, the optical reflection law from $\sigma$ defines a (partially defined) symplectomorphism $T_\sigma$ on $\Pi$: an incoming oriented line is sent to the corresponding reflected oriented line. Reflection from $\gamma$ itself is denoted $T_\gamma$.

Question: Is it true that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, every $C^\infty$ Hamiltonian symplectomorphism $\Pi \to \Pi$ can be approximated, in the $C^\infty$ topology on compact subsets of its domain, by finite compositions
$$T_{\sigma_N} \circ T_{\sigma_{N-1}} \circ \cdots \circ T_{\sigma_1},$$
where each $\sigma_j$ is either $\gamma$ itself or a closed hypersurface that is $\varepsilon$-close to $\gamma$ in the $C^k$ topology, and where only the reflection maps $T_{\sigma_j}$ themselves (and not their inverses) are allowed in the compositions?
artifact.status_search_result: A. Glutsyuk (Israel J. Math., 2023; arXiv:2005.02657) proved the analogous density result for the pseudogroup generated by compositional ratios of reflections from $\gamma$ and from its small deformations — that is, allowing both reflections and their inverses. The variant restricting to reflections only (without inverses) is listed as an open problem in the open-problems compilation on billiards and geometric optics, and no resolution is found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Density of thin film billiard reflection pseudogroup in Hamiltonian symplectomorphism pseudogroup
status_evidence.snippet: The pseudogroup generated by compositional ratios of reflections from a convex hypersurface and from its small deformations is C∞-dense in the pseudogroup of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms between subdomains of the phase cylinder.
status_evidence.claim: Glutsyuk's theorem establishes density using compositional ratios (reflections together with their inverses), not reflections alone.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Billiards and Geometric Optics
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of whether each Hamiltonian symplectomorphism of Π is a C∞-limit of compositions of reflections from γ and from hypersurfaces ε-close to γ.
status_evidence.claim: The reflections-only version is recorded as an open question.
